title: Representation Learning Enables Scalable Multitask Deep Reinforcement Learning
claim: Adding predictive model-based representations lets performance keep improving with network size, while the plain baseline stays flat or degrades as capacity grows.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, learning curves, shared legend inside right panel
description: Two line-plot panels, HalfCheetah on the left and Humanoid on the right. Each plots evaluation episodic return (×10^3) against environment steps from 0 to 1M. Two method families appear as two color families. PPO is drawn with dashed red lines and triangle markers. PPO plus MB. Representations is drawn with solid teal/blue lines and circle markers. Shade encodes network size from Small (light) to X-Large (dark), as the legend inside the right panel shows. Noisy curves have faint confidence bands. In HalfCheetah the teal curves reach about 3–3.8k, well above PPO at about 1.5–2.8k. In Humanoid the light-teal Small curve climbs steeply past 3k, and the larger models do less well. PPO curves stay near 0.5–0.8k. The eye goes first to the teal curves rising above the red ones.
caption: Representation quality drives scaling performance in model-free RL. We compare standard PPO with a variant augmented with model-based representations (+\,MB.\ Representations) across four network sizes (Small, Medium, Large, X-Large) on HalfCheetah and Humanoid.
abstract: Scaling reinforcement learning (RL) to diverse multitask settings remains a central challenge. While recent advances in model-based RL achieve strong performance, they rely on planning and complex training pipelines, making it unclear which components are essential for scalability. We revisit this question and argue that the primary driver of scalable multitask RL is not model-based control, but \emph{representation learning}. In particular, we show that combining predictive, model-based representations with high-capacity value function approximation is sufficient to achieve strong performance, even without planning. We evaluate a simple model-free algorithm, MR.Q, coupled with auxiliary predictive objectives into a scalable actor-critic architecture. This approach outperforms a recent world-model-based method and a range of deep RL baselines across a diverse suite of multitask continuous control tasks, while significantly reducing computational overhead and improving wall-clock efficiency. We observe consistent improvements with increased model capacity and show through ablations that predictive representation learning is critical for performance.
